english.title: Lend insurance document with intent to deceive
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) with intent to deceive, lent

(A)_[a certificate of insurance]_
(B)_[a document produced as evidence of insurance pursuant to regulation 6 of the Motor Vehicle (Compulsory Insurance) (No. 2) Regulations 1973]_
(C)_[a document issued under regulations made under section 165(2)(a) of the Road Traffic Act 1988]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 173(1)(b) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
with intent to deceive
lent insurance document

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Until 1st November 2021, securities or deposits could be used as an alternative to conventional motor insurance. For offences before that date see H3016

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
